images.title: A 5 × 3 grid with the top right square removed
images.purpose: Show a 5 × 3 grid with its top right square removed, tiled with 7 tiles.
images.composition: One grid in the centre: 5 rows and 3 columns, taller than wide.
exact_structure: A grid of 5 rows and 3 columns of equal squares; the top right square is missing, drawn as a dashed empty outline with the small word removed inside it.
Exactly 7 tiles of 2 squares each, with thick dark outlines, covering the other 14 squares.
Row 1: one horizontal tile over columns 1 and 2.
Rows 2 and 3: one vertical tile in column 3 over rows 2 and 3, and one horizontal tile over columns 1 and 2 of row 2, and one over columns 1 and 2 of row 3.
Rows 4 and 5: one vertical tile in each of columns 1, 2 and 3, each over rows 4 and 5.
Tiles are filled alternately teal (#0072B2) and amber (#E69F00).
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: This 14 square region can be tiled, by placing tiles one at a time.
images.description: Show a 5 × 3 grid with its top right square removed, tiled with 7 tiles.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.

image_decisions.why: Students need to see that an even count of squares can be tiled here before meeting a case that cannot.
